title: Attack and defend: SQL injection
blurb: See why mixing input into SQL is dangerous, find injection attempts in web logs, and fix it in code and at the firewall.
scenario: The DMZ web shop's logs show odd requests to the product page, and the database team saw an unusual query. Work out whether this is SQL injection, fix the root cause with the developers, and add network protection while the fix ships.
objectives: Choose the root-cause fix and the compensating controls

steps.title: Where the flaw is
steps.learn: **SQL injection** happens when an application builds a database query by **pasting user input into the SQL text**. Input that contains SQL syntax then changes the query's logic. It's #3 (Injection) in the OWASP Top 10 (2021).
steps.question: Which line of server code is vulnerable?

options.text: query = "SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = '" + request.id + "'"

options.why: That's a parameterized query. The input is sent as data, never as SQL.
Converting to an integer rejects any SQL text, which is a good extra check.

steps.title: Spot the attempts
steps.task: Pick every log line that shows an injection attempt.
steps.question: Web access log, product page:

options.text: GET /product?id=42 UNION SELECT username,password FROM users--

steps.title: Fix it properly
steps.learn: The **root-cause fix** is in the code. Network controls are **compensating**: they buy time and catch known patterns, but encoded or new variants can slip past.

fields.label: Snort SQL injection rules in the FTD intrusion policy
Database account with only the rights the app needs

steps.title: Turn on IPS protection
steps.learn: FTD can only inspect what it can see. HTTPS to the web server must be **decrypted** (with the server's key, a "known key" SSL rule) before Snort can match injection patterns in it.
steps.task: Add an SSL rule with the **Decrypt - Known Key** action for the web server, and set the intrusion policy on the web rule to **Security Over Connectivity**.
steps.screen: FMC › Policies › SSL and Access Control

summary: Concatenated SQL as the flaw, tautology, UNION and time-delay patterns in logs, parameterized queries as the fix, least privilege and IPS as compensating controls, and decryption so the IPS can see inside HTTPS.
